title: First-run setup and server commands that read the recorded settings
spec: crewcraft-server first-run <data-dir> --name <server-name> --admin <email> [--listen <address:port>] creates a new installation (never an existing directory, refused before anything else is asked), writes trust-root.der and server.conf (name and listen address, owner-only on Unix), then invites the administrator. The code is shown only in a private interactive terminal, so without one first-run refuses before creating anything. It prints the root SHA-256 and the invitation as crewcraft://enroll?server=<name:port>&code=<code>&root_sha256=<hex> (values percent-encoded for a query, so IPv6 brackets are %5B and %5D) and the parts separately. The default listen address is 127.0.0.1:7443; port 0 is refused because invitations carry the port. server.conf is key = value lines with # comments; both keys are required once and any other key is refused. serve <data-dir> serves with the recorded name and address until interrupted; invite <data-dir> <email>, room <data-dir> <owner> <name> and add-member <data-dir> <room> <owner> <member> open the same installation, pinned to trust-root.der. The lab commands are unchanged.
